title: Philip IV to Cardinal Albornoz, Madrid, 24 July 1648 (catalogue 747): keep the nuncio Rospigliosi, the future Clement IX; key rebuilt from a 1649 plain copy

steps.what: Inventory of the 69 shelfmarks of no. 747 on PARES: four are digitised (CT.2,D.16, CT.2,D.20, CT.2,D.32, CT.11,D.1).
Prior work: catalogue, this repository, Cryptiana, Arriazu García 2024, web: no reading of CT.2,D.32.
K1 rebuilt from CT.2,D.16 cipher aligned on its contemporary plain copy; frozen.
K1 on held-out CT.2,D.20 (transcribed before its plain copy was opened): 0.638 of characters vs control p99 0.550. Family key: number series shifted.
K1 applied to CT.2,D.32: the 1648 letter is in a different cipher (syllable tokens ne, mo, ma, so, ri; numbers 2-61).
Same cipher found in CT.11,D.1 image 3 (1649), with its plain copy (image 1); repeat "dentro de Cataluña y" opened the alignment; K2 learnt on lines 1-12 and frozen.
K2 on held-out lines 13-23: 0.859 of characters vs 200 permuted-value controls, median 0.419, p99 0.476.
Both copies of CT.2,D.32 transcribed and decoded with K2; additions K2b (each attested at least twice or fitting a series); copies compared group by group.

Claude Opus 5.5 (PR review on merge): the plain copies of the time used to rebuild K1 and K2 credited (contemporary); method kept as plaintext from external sources (the copies are in other files of the Osuna fonds, not beside the 1648 letter).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 636 tokens, 84 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.038 per letter; random keys -3.743 (z 11.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.535 (mean -2.565, z 19.3); annealer on the real text -2.246. Verdict: pass.
Claude Opus 5.5 (PR review on merge): D.32 graded A; the three key documents listed as not-prose texts.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.038; polyphony 0.0; 7 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.246

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Key K2 rebuilt from another document in the same cipher (OSUNA,CT.11,D.1, 1649) and its contemporary plain copy, validated on held-out lines, then applied to the 1648 letter.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Copy B: 353 of 359 groups with a value (98.3%), about 5 of them probable; 6 unresolved. 6 of 136 words of the cipher portion contain a hole.

credits.note: keys K1 and K2 rebuilt and validated on held-out text; both cipher copies of the 1648 letter read, Spanish text and English translation
the plain copies of the time filed with OSUNA,CT.11,D.1 (Haro to Peñaranda, 25 Sept 1649, enciphered for Albornoz; key K2) and with CT.2,D.16 and D.20 (1644-45; key K1)

texts.label: Philip IV to Cardinal Albornoz, Madrid, 24 July 1648 (AHNOB OSUNA,CT.2,D.32)
texts.summary: In 1648 Innocent X was renewing his nuncios. Philip IV wanted to keep his own: Giulio Rospigliosi, Archbishop of Tarsus, nuncio at Madrid since 1644 – the future Pope Clement IX. He wrote so to his ambassador to the Pope, Cardinal Gil de Albornoz, in a cipher nobody had read: “there can be no instrument more suitable” for the service of both courts, so the ambassador must not desist “in any case”. The letter survives in two ciphered copies with no decipherment; the key came from another paper in the same family archive, a chapter of a letter by Luis de Haro enciphered for Albornoz in 1649, whose plain-text copy was kept.

reading_review.note: reading.md read against translation.md and the decryption lines of copy B: three coherent sentences of chancery Spanish (the request on the Archbishop of Tarsus and the Pope's answer; the King's insistence that the ambassador press for Rospigliosi's retention and not desist; the order to report). The holes are the four code signs (74, underlined A, 124 twice, cross-11) and the doubtful "el"; four of them fall in the first sentence, which still parses (Veo [que] pasastis los oficios con Su Santidad, y lo que [el] respondió ...). The rest is continuous; probable readings {b}, {o}, {Be} and restorations [que], [de] are marked. Lines B09-B13 of the transcription (the reveal passage) were compared with image 5 at the published resolution and agree.

texts.label: OSUNA,CT.11,D.1: Haro to Peñaranda, 25 Sept 1649, enciphered for Albornoz, with its plain copy of the time (key document for K2)
texts.summary: Key document: the cipher chapter and its plain copy of the time, used to rebuild K2 (lines 1-12) and to test it (lines 13-23); no reading of its own.

texts.label: OSUNA,CT.2,D.16: Philip IV to Albornoz, 12 Dec 1644, cipher aligned on its plain copy (key document for K1)
texts.summary: Key document: cipher original aligned on the plain copy of the time, used to rebuild K1, which does not read the 1648 letter.

texts.label: OSUNA,CT.2,D.20: Philip IV to Albornoz, 26 Jan 1645, cipher and plain copy (test of K1)
texts.summary: Key document: transcribed before its plain copy was opened, used to test K1 (0.638 of characters recovered against a 99th percentile of 0.550 for permuted keys).

prior.where: Catalogue 747 open; nothing on the Osuna fonds in this repository; Cryptiana's Spanish ciphers stop about 1519; X. Arriazu García's thesis on Albornoz (2024) cites other Osuna cipher letters, not this one; web search 28 Oct 2026.

human: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
